title: Client Query, Cache, and Privacy Semantics
authorityBoundary: This artefact defines semantic requirements for app-surface privacy classification, consent and audit posture, query view mapping, and cache invalidation. It does not create legal conclusions, compliance certification, privacy policy publication, store submission, provider integration, cache implementation, query library setup, list/detail/search implementation, renderer implementation, product UI readiness, cache readiness, sync readiness, store readiness, production readiness, live-provider readiness, monetisation readiness, or human acceptance.

clientStateSynchronisationSemantics.rule: Client state and data-synchronisation behaviours must be USF-defined and must map server state, UI-only state, persistent local state, offline posture, sync queues, cache invalidation, revalidation, multi-device consistency, realtime subscriptions, background refresh, retention, purge, and shared-device posture to capability semantics before implementation.

stateClasses.description: Data obtained from governed USF queries or subscriptions.
Local presentation state with no authority over business behaviour.
Device or browser retained state that requires retention, purge, shared-device, and privacy posture.
Evaluated command or workflow intent that must preserve idempotency, conflict, retry, tenant, privacy, and audit semantics.
Cached query projection governed by cache, invalidation, revalidation, stale data, tenant isolation, and privacy purge semantics.
Realtime projection governed by event, permission, privacy, audit, lifecycle, recovery, and proof semantics.
Background refresh posture governed by platform constraints, permission, privacy, cache, telemetry, and proof semantics.
State visible on shared or privacy-sensitive devices governed by purge, logout, session expiry, redaction, and proof semantics.

mustReject: state class without USF definition
offline behaviour without capability mapping
cache behaviour without invalidation mapping
persistent local state without retention and purge mapping
shared-device state without privacy and purge mapping
sync behaviour without proof expectation

serverClientStateClassification.rule: Server state and client state must be classified before any app-surface storage, cache, query, synchronization, or UI state implementation is accepted.

serverStateDefinition.description: Server state is data whose source of truth is governed by USF query, command, event, subscription, or semantic contract authority outside the local app surface.

clientStateDefinition.description: Client state is local presentation, session, persistence, cache, offline, or device/browser state that must not redefine server-side capability, permission, validation, audit, or lifecycle semantics.

classificationBoundaries: UI-only state must not define business behaviour.
Cached server state remains server state and must preserve freshness, staleness, tenant, privacy, and purge mappings.
Persistent client state requires retention, purge, shared-device, and privacy posture before implementation.
Offline queued mutations are client-held intents and must still map to command authority, idempotency, conflict, audit, privacy, and proof semantics.
Unknown or mixed state classes must fail closed until explicitly classified.
mustReject: state without server-or-client classification
client state defining capability behaviour
cached server state without freshness or purge mapping
persistent client state without retention and privacy mapping
offline intent without command authority mapping
state implementation readiness claim without proof

privacySemanticFoundation.rule: App-surface privacy, consent, disclosure, and international compliance semantics must be derived from USF capabilities and semantic contracts, with store disclosure requirements represented as requirements only and never as compliance claims.
privacySemanticFoundation.storeDisclosurePosture: Store disclosure impact must be represented for each relevant client data surface without claiming Apple privacy compliance, Google Play Data Safety compliance, ATT compliance, international compliance, or store readiness.
privacySemanticFoundation.consentAndAuditPosture: Consent purpose, consent receipt, audit event, actor, tenant boundary, retention, deletion, export, redaction, and proof requirements must be identified before any privacy, consent, store, ads, analytics, diagnostics, or SDK usage claim is accepted.

cacheInvalidationSemantics.rule: Client cache invalidation must be capability and event driven, tenant-safe, privacy-aware, and explicit about stale data, revalidation triggers, mutation outcomes, privacy purge, and user messaging.
mustReject: cache rule without capability mapping
cache invalidation without event mapping
privacy purge without privacy data category mapping
tenant-scoped cache without tenant isolation mapping
stale data display without user messaging posture

clientPrivacyClassification.rule: Every client field and event must have a privacy classification requirement before implementation or store disclosure claims.
mustReject: field without privacy classification requirement
event without privacy classification requirement
telemetry without privacy mapping
diagnostic payload without privacy mapping
notification payload without privacy mapping
ad event without consent purpose mapping
store disclosure value without semantic backing

queryViewModelMapping.rule: Query-driven list, detail, and search views must map to USF query authority, cache posture, privacy, permissions, i18n, accessibility, telemetry, and proof before implementation.

cacheInvalidationByCapabilityAndEvent.rule: Cache invalidation must identify the capability, event, affected query keys, affected view models, tenant scope, privacy purge effect, revalidation trigger, proof expectation, and implementation block.
mustReject: event without cache invalidation posture
mutation outcome without affected query key mapping
privacy purge without affected view model mapping
tenant-scoped event without tenant cache isolation mapping

validatorRequirements.description: Reject client state, cache, sync, persistence, offline, background refresh, realtime subscription, or shared-device behaviour without USF state class, capability, privacy, retention, purge, validator, and proof mappings.
Reject app-surface state without explicit server-state or client-state classification, authority boundary, privacy posture, freshness or retention mapping where applicable, and proof expectation.
Reject privacy labels, data safety statements, consent flows, SDK usage, store disclosure values, or client data surfaces without USF semantic backing and evidence requirements.
Reject cache rules without capability, event, privacy, tenant isolation, stale data, revalidation, and proof mappings.
Reject client fields, events, telemetry, diagnostics, notifications, storage, or ad events without privacy category, consent purpose where applicable, store disclosure impact, and proof mappings.
Reject query-driven list, detail, or search views without query, cache, privacy, permission, i18n, accessibility, telemetry, and proof mappings.
Reject cache invalidation records without capability, event, affected query key, affected view model, tenant scope, privacy purge, revalidation trigger, stale data message, and proof mappings.

proofRequirements.description: Future proof must demonstrate that query views, cache invalidation, and client field or event privacy classifications are projections of governed USF capabilities and fail closed when mappings are absent.

Future proof must demonstrate that every state entry is classified as server state, UI-only state, persistent local state, offline queue, cached query state, realtime subscription state, background refresh state, or shared-device state, and that unknown or mixed state classes fail closed.

Future proof must demonstrate that store disclosure, consent, privacy label, Data Safety, ATT, ads, analytics, diagnostics, and SDK usage artefacts cannot claim compliance or readiness without explicit semantic backing, evidence, and owner acceptance.

implementationEvaluationRequirements: client query, cache, and privacy mappings exist for the relevant capability
validator requirements are implemented and selftested

proof evidence exists for mapped and rejected query, cache, and privacy cases
owner acceptance is recorded before any compliance, store, cache, sync, query, product UI, or readiness claim
